theme: The insider checklist — what 1,500 events taught us about what actually fails

linkedin.text:
16 years. 1,500+ events. 130+ destinations. 25,000+ participants.

That volume buys you something no planning checklist can: a pattern library of what actually breaks.

Here are 3 operational truths that took us years to learn — shared peer-to-peer because every HR or Marketing leader running a global incentive programme deserves to know them:

→ The brief describes the group. The group is never the brief. Edge cases in dietary needs, accessibility, and connectivity requirements show up at 2x the projected rate, every time.

→ 'Confirmed' and 'contracted' are not synonyms in 27 of the 130+ countries we operate in. The paper exists; the room does not. Always verify on-site.

→ The transfer is the event. A 90-minute bus ride with no water, no audio, and no agenda is the experience your team remembers — not the keynote that followed.

What's the operational lesson that surprised you most when planning a large-scale corporate event? Genuinely curious — reply below.

instagram.text:
1,500+ events. 130+ destinations. Here's what actually breaks corporate incentive trips. 🧳

❌ Trusting venue photos over site inspections
❌ Underestimating transfer time between 'nearby' points on a map
❌ Budgeting for the group average, ignoring the edge cases
❌ Treating the agenda as fixed when the weather, airline, or minister of tourism has other plans
✅ Building in the contingency before the client ever knows it was needed

The gap between a great event and a forgettable one isn't budget. It's operational precision built from repetition.

From business to pleasure — without the avoidable turbulence.

facebook.text:
After producing 1,500+ corporate events across 130+ destinations, here are 3 things we've watched derail otherwise perfect incentive trips — shared here because we've paid for this knowledge so you don't have to:

1️⃣ The 'trust the local vendor' assumption. Great local partners exist. Vetting them at speed, under a corporate brief, in a language you don't speak — that's where costs explode.

2️⃣ Confusing a beautiful venue with a functional one. A rooftop with a view and a rooftop that seats 300 for a gala dinner are two completely different buildings.

3️⃣ Logistics planned for the average participant. 25,000+ participants taught us that the edge cases — dietary, mobility, connectivity — are never as rare as the brief suggests.

Anything on this list hit close to home? Tell us in the comments. And if you're in planning mode, DM us — we're happy to sanity-check a brief.
